Welcome to Accessible HTML5

This is a well-structured, accessible HTML5 document demonstrating modern best practices for semantic markup and inclusive design.

It uses semantic landmarks, a skip link for keyboard navigation, and CSS that adapts to your light or dark mode preference.

Text and link colors meet WCAG AA contrast in both themes, type scales with your browser's font size, and motion respects your system settings.

Features

  • Semantic HTML structure with proper landmarks
  • Keyboard accessible navigation and focus management
  • Dark mode support with custom color schemes
  • Responsive typography using modern CSS
  • Print-friendly styles for better readability
  • WCAG AA contrast compliance in all color modes

Examples

Component Cards

Card components are useful for organizing related content. They include a subtle border and padding for visual separation.

Learn more about accessibility resources

Interactive Elements

Buttons and links are fully accessible with clear focus states. All interactive elements include visible focus indicators and proper ARIA labels.

Keyboard navigation: Use Tab to move forward, Shift+Tab to move backward, and Enter or Space to activate.

Accessible Form

content.text:
I fixed three real defects in `0.html`; the file was already in good shape, so I left the rest alone. Nothing was tested in a browser or screen reader — these are edits from reading the code.

## What changed

- **Invalid `<noscript>` markup**: a `<style>` sat inside a `<noscript>` in the body, which is not valid HTML. The styles now live in a `<noscript>` in the `<head>`, and the notice is a plain paragraph with a class instead of an inline `style` attribute.
- **Broken layout without JavaScript**: the notice was a direct child of `<body>`, which is a three-row grid, so it pushed the header into the stretching row and the main content out of place. It now sits inside the header.
- **Counter announced twice**: the `<output>` was a live region and so was the "Count is N." message below it, so screen readers heard every change twice. The `<output>` is now `aria-live="off"` and linked to its buttons with `for`; the message below does the announcing. I updated the card's description to match.

## Smaller no-JavaScript touches

- The empty dashed live-region boxes are now hidden when JavaScript is off.
- The notice now says the contact form is unavailable, because the page's content security policy (`form-action 'none'`) blocks a native submit and the form would otherwise fail silently.

## Left alone

- **Placeholder URLs**: the canonical link and `og:url` still point to `https://www.example.com`, and the footer GitHub link goes to `https://github.com`. Swap in the real URLs before publishing.
- **Duplicated dark palette**: the dark colours are declared twice, once for the system preference and once for the manual override. `light-dark()` would remove the duplication, but it drops support for browsers from before 2024, and the file otherwise takes care to provide fallbacks.
- **Invalid email submit is noisy**: the form status, the inline error and the focus move each announce something. It is redundant rather than wrong, so I didn't change it.
